summary: Performance analysis of PRODDB during peak hour. Identified 3 issues requiring immediate attention.

findings.description: Buffer cache hit ratio is 87.75%, well below 95% target for OLTP. Physical reads total 6,655,654 against logical reads of 54,200,745. db file sequential read is the dominant wait event at 89,931 seconds total wait time.
findings.root_cause: DB_CACHE_SIZE at 512 MB is undersized for this workload. Physical I/O dominates the wait profile.
findings.recommendation: Increase DB_CACHE_SIZE to 640 MB. V$DB_CACHE_ADVICE shows physical read factor drops to 0.720 at this size, a significant 28% reduction in estimated physical reads.

findings.description: Redo subsystem showing heavy contention. log file sync waits: 2,156,789 waits totaling 6,470 seconds. log file parallel write: 2,109,834 waits totaling 4,220 seconds. Combined redo-related wait time is 10,690 seconds, making it the second largest wait category after User I/O.
findings.root_cause: Redo logging infrastructure cannot keep up with transaction volume of ~36 transactions/second. This is a critical bottleneck consuming 21% of total foreground wait time.
findings.recommendation: Add additional redo log groups to reduce log file sync frequency. Increase LOG_BUFFER beyond 16 MB. Migrate redo logs to dedicated NVMe storage to reduce log file parallel write latency.

findings.description: PGA cache hit percentage is 88.9%, below 95% target. Over allocation count is 5,847. In-memory sort ratio is 98.09% meaning 1.91% of sorts spill to disk.
findings.root_cause: PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET at 512 MB is insufficient for the current sort and hash join workload. Work areas are spilling to temporary tablespace.
findings.recommendation: Increase PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET to 768 MB. V$PGA_TARGET_ADVICE shows over-allocation drops to 412 and cache hit reaches 97.7% at this size. This represents a good cost-benefit tradeoff.
